decisions.reason: As a core bread item that is very close to the established bakery range, it likely requires little new investment and management would usually retain it unless there were clear sustained signs of weak demand.

The guided historic mill tour involves visible commitment to the firm's heritage and hospitality positioning, and disappointing recent years can readily be treated as temporary rather than a reason to reverse course.

This farmhouse bread fits the traditional assortment, but as a less publicly committed line extension with no reported standout result it is somewhat more exposed to later assortment pruning than the more symbolic offers.

The poppy seed Christmas stollen was publicly presented as a flagship and carries an award signal, so sunk commitment, reputational visibility, and strategic centrality all strongly favor continuing it.

The premium Christmas stollen is close to the seasonal core offer and supported by an award, so management would be reluctant to withdraw it absent unmistakable failure even though it is less central than the flagship stollen.
